1	# Architecture - notes
2	
3	A fourth kind of design, besides features, the design system and the shell:
4	**the project's architecture**, kept as markdown files that agents read and
5	shown to the team on the project's Architecture pages, the way the design
6	system's gallery shows the system. Prelude's own architecture (from
7	`CLAUDE.md` and `docs/plan.md`) is the sample data.
8	
9	This design is those pages: views at Prelude's own URLs
10	(`/f/:folder/architecture/…`), with states shaped as Prelude's model of the
11	files would be.
12	
13	## Decided (2026-10-22, with the person)
14	
15	- **A design of `"kind": "architecture"`, one per project** (R-p0j), like the
16	  system and the shell. Its sessions shape it ("draft it from the code").
17	- **Prelude reads the files itself**, as it reads RULES.md, so nothing is
18	  written twice (D-e8y in the sample). The real architecture design will
19	  have no states; this design's states stand in for what Prelude reads.
20	- **Markdown, a file per thing**, in the design's `architecture/` folder (as
21	  the system's is `system/`):
22	  - `overview.md`: a summary, the layers in order, the principles (title, why);
23	  - `parts/<id>.md`: a header (title, layer, kind: module / process / outside,
24	    `files` globs, `uses` part ids), then sections: Responsible for, Not its
25	    job, Owns;
26	  - `decisions/<id>.md`: a header (title, status, date, parts, supersedes),
27	    then Context, Decision, Consequences. Ids are `D-` + three random
28	    characters, so branches never clash;
29	  - `flows/<id>.md`: a title, a summary, numbered steps each starting with
30	    the part's id.
31	  Prelude prepares what's derived: each part's "used by", decisions and
32	  findings, and the map's layers.
33	- **Proposed decisions are accepted by merging** (R-7tq): an agent's
34	  proposal is reviewed with its branch, and Prelude marks it accepted at
35	  merge (as it clears a route's `from`).
36	- **Agents use it** (R-c2m, R-h9w): ever

text:
1	# Rules: Architecture
2	
3	- **R-p0j.** A project has one architecture at most, as it has one design system and one app shell.
4	- **R-c2m.** Every design, build and fix agent reads the architecture's principles, and the parts its change reaches, before it changes anything.
5	  *shown-on: /f/:folder/architecture*
6	- **R-h9w.** An agent whose change would go against the architecture proposes a decision on its branch, rather than making the change without saying so.
7	- **R-7tq.** A proposed decision is accepted when the branch that proposed it is merged into main, and agents on other branches don't see it before then.
8	  *shown-on: /f/:folder/architecture/decisions/:decision*
9	- **R-4vx.** After every turn that changes code, the changed files are checked against the architecture, and a build or fix agent is told what doesn't match with its next message.
10	  *shown-on: /f/:folder/architecture @ drifted*
11	- **R-k5e.** A part may use the parts its file says it may, in its own layer or below it; any other use is reported, and so is a file no part names or a named file that isn't there.
12	  *shown-on: /f/:folder/architecture/parts/:part @ drifted*
13	- **R-w8d.** Decisions are listed newest first.
14	  *shown-on: /f/:folder/architecture/decisions*

1	# Prelude architecture
2	
3	Prelude is a tool for designing and then building an app with an agent: you pick a project, chat with the Claude Code CLI, and watch the design appear beside the chat. It runs as one Node server (plain `node:http`, views in Eta, Koda in the page) on localhost:4200, optionally inside a Tauri desktop window. Everything it produces is files in the project's `prelude/` folder, each design worked on in its own git branch and worktree. Agent-written views render in a sandboxed child process, and each design is served on its own preview origin.
4	
5	## Layers
6	
7	1. Windows
8	2. Entry points
9	3. Pages
10	4. Agent and live state
11	5. Designs and hosting
12	6. Project files
13	7. Shared helpers
14	8. Outside
15	
16	## Principles
17	
18	- **The folder is the database.** Everything Prelude makes is a file under the project's `prelude/`, committed with the code; `~/.prelude/` holds only machine-local conveniences, so nothing is lost if it's deleted.
19	- **The server is the single source of truth for live state.** Every window (chat, pop-out, browser tab) renders from the server and re-renders on its SSE events, so no window holds state another needs.
20	- **Agent-written code never runs in the server's process.** A design's views render in a sandboxed renderer, and a host that runs them unsandboxed starts only once the person approves it.
21	- **The agent works with ordinary file tools, fenced to what it may touch.** It reads the project and the folders added as references, writes only where its mode allows, and deletes by writing a file empty.
22	- **A design's memory is its files, not a conversation.** Each session starts from NOTES.md, the views and states, so sessions on different machines and branches pick up where the work stands.
23	- **Committed files must merge cleanly.** Session folders and decision ids are random, transcripts are append-only, and there's no shared index that every session rewrites.

7	
8	Prelude's server: plain `node:http` with every route in `server/main.js`, started by `start.js`. It follows Koda's contract, answering each URL as a whole page or as a fragment, and wires the other parts together for each request and each turn.
9	
10	## Responsible for
11	- Routing, and refusing POSTs that don't come from Prelude's own origin
12	- Starting turns with the right prompt, mode and permissions, and what follows a turn (review, commit, drift check)
13	- Sending requests for a design's origin to the host
14	
15	## Not its job
16	- Building page models or rendering agent-written views
17	- Talking to the CLI or git directly
18	
19	## Owns
20	- The in-memory app: folders, channels, turns, renderers, hosts and runs it created

**What I changed**

- **`server/main.js`**: a new route after the part route, built the same way. It takes the flow by id from the architecture's model. A fragment request from a page in the app layout gets the view alone; a cold load gets the page in the app layout. An id that no flow has gets a 404 ("The architecture has no such flow.").
